title: Term Exam — General Science Term 3
revision: 2026-11 rev2 — 70:30 LOTS:HOTS, balanced choices, in-scope items only

questions.text: Which gas makes up about 21% of Earth's atmosphere?
options: Oxygen
Nitrogen gas
Carbon dioxide
Argon gas
questions.correct: Oxygen

questions.text: What generates Earth's magnetic field?
options: Its molten iron outer core
The ozone layer high above
Magnetic rocks in mountains
The ocean tides near coasts
questions.correct: Its molten iron outer core

questions.text: Why does ice floating on lakes help aquatic life?
options: It insulates the water below
It adds oxygen to the water
It makes the water much saltier
It reflects heat down to the fish
questions.correct: It insulates the water below

questions.text: Why is water called essential for life?
options: It dissolves substances for cell reactions
It is the only source of energy for living cells
It makes up the whole of Earth's crust
It blocks all harmful light from the Sun
questions.correct: It dissolves substances for cell reactions

questions.text: Which planet has a thin, cold CO₂ atmosphere and polar ice caps?
options: Mars
Venus
Mercury
Neptune
questions.correct: Mars

questions.text: Earth and the Moon are the same distance from the Sun, yet the Moon swings from very hot to very cold. What BEST explains this?
options: The Moon has almost no atmosphere to hold heat
The Moon is much closer to the Sun than Earth
The Moon has a thick atmosphere of carbon dioxide
The Moon has oceans that boil away each day
questions.correct: The Moon has almost no atmosphere to hold heat

questions.text: What happens to infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface?
options: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit some
All of it escapes straight into space at once
It is turned into visible light by the clouds
It is stored forever inside the ozone layer
questions.correct: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit some

questions.text: Which activity adds nitrous oxide to the atmosphere?
options: Heavy use of nitrogen fertilizers
Planting fruit trees in backyards
Using solar panels in schools
Collecting rainwater in barrels
questions.correct: Heavy use of nitrogen fertilizers

questions.text: What is the difference between the natural and enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: The enhanced one is extra warming from human gases
The natural effect is caused only by humans burning fuel
The enhanced effect cools the Earth by blocking sunlight
There is no difference; both terms mean the same thing
questions.correct: The enhanced one is extra warming from human gases

questions.text: Why does deforestation strengthen the greenhouse effect?
options: Fewer trees remove CO₂, and burning adds more
Trees release most of the methane in the air we breathe
Forests reflect all sunlight back into space
Cutting trees makes the soil absorb more CO₂
questions.correct: Fewer trees remove CO₂, and burning adds more

questions.text: A family switches from a 100 W bulb to a 15 W LED with the same brightness. How does this help the climate?
options: Less electricity used means less fuel burned
It makes the house brighter, so the Sun shines less
LEDs absorb carbon dioxide from the air inside the room
LEDs produce oxygen while they are turned on
questions.correct: Less electricity used means less fuel burned

questions.text: Ice cores show that CO₂ levels and temperature rose and fell together over thousands of years. What does this support?
options: CO₂ and temperature are closely linked
CO₂ has no effect on Earth's climate
Temperature is controlled only by the Moon
Ice cores are not useful for science
questions.correct: CO₂ and temperature are closely linked

questions.text: What drives the slow movement of tectonic plates?
options: Mantle heat currents and sinking slabs
Ocean tides pulling hard on the continents
Strong typhoon winds over the islands
Rivers carrying sediment to the sea
questions.correct: Mantle heat currents and sinking slabs

questions.text: What happens at a divergent boundary?
options: Plates move apart and new crust forms
Plates collide and one sinks below
Plates slide past each other sideways
Plates stay still and never move
questions.correct: Plates move apart and new crust forms

questions.text: Which plate sinks beneath the Philippines along the Philippine Trench?
options: Philippine Sea Plate
African Plate
Antarctic Plate (south)
Nazca Plate
questions.correct: Philippine Sea Plate

questions.text: Why does the Philippine Fault Zone produce strong earthquakes?
options: Blocks lock, then suddenly slip
Magma always flows out along the fault line
The fault is filled with water that shakes
Volcanoes push the fault open every year
questions.correct: Blocks lock, then suddenly slip

questions.text: A line of volcanoes runs parallel to a deep trench in eastern Mindanao. What process connects them?
options: Subduction at the trench produces magma for the volcanoes
The trench collects rainwater that erupts from the volcanoes
The volcanoes dig the trench as lava flows into the sea
The trench and volcanoes formed by unrelated processes
questions.correct: Subduction at the trench produces magma for the volcanoes

questions.text: A website says the Philippines formed all at once from one giant volcano. Which evaluation is BEST?
options: Wrong — it formed over millions of years, in many ways
Correct — one volcano built all 7,600 islands in a day
Correct — the islands were created by a single typhoon
Wrong — the islands were formed by ice age glaciers only
questions.correct: Wrong — it formed over millions of years, in many ways

questions.text: About how many tropical cyclones enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility each year?
options: About 20
About 2
About 50
About 100
questions.correct: About 20

questions.text: Which island is the only natural home of the tamaraw?
options: Mindoro
Palawan
Bohol
Batanes
questions.correct: Mindoro

questions.text: What climate does the Philippines have?
options: Tropical maritime
Polar and icy
Desert and dry
Temperate with snow
questions.correct: Tropical maritime

questions.text: Why are many species in the Philippines found nowhere else?
options: Islands kept populations isolated
The country is connected to all continents
Animals were brought from other countries
The climate is too cold for most species
questions.correct: Islands kept populations isolated

questions.text: A tourist wants to see karst landscapes in the Philippines. Which places should she visit?
options: El Nido and the Underground River
Mayon and Taal volcano craters
Central Luzon's flat rice plains
Tubbataha's open-ocean coral atolls
questions.correct: El Nido and the Underground River

questions.text: Why do mountain ranges like the Sierra Madre hold some of the country's last large forests and endemic species?
options: Steep, wet, hard-to-reach terrain limited clearing
Mountains are always too dry for farming of any kind
Laws allow logging only in the lowland areas
Endemic species cannot live below 2,000 meters
questions.correct: Steep, wet, hard-to-reach terrain limited clearing

questions.text: What is a mineral?
options: Natural inorganic solid, definite makeup
Any rock found at the bottom of a river
Soil made from leaves and decaying plants
Liquid metal found deep in Earth's core
questions.correct: Natural inorganic solid, definite makeup

questions.text: Which igneous rock is light enough to float because of trapped gas bubbles?
options: Pumice
Granite
Marble
Shale
questions.correct: Pumice

questions.text: How does sedimentary rock form?
options: Sediments compact and cement together
Magma cools slowly underground
Heat and pressure change other rock types
Lava cools very quickly in water
questions.correct: Sediments compact and cement together

questions.text: Why is copper widely used in electrical wiring?
options: It conducts electricity well
It is the hardest of all metals
It never needs to be mined
It does not conduct electricity
questions.correct: It conducts electricity well

questions.text: A sculptor wants a stone that is smooth, can be polished, and is found locally. Which should she choose?
options: Marble from Romblon
Pumice from Pinatubo
Sandstone from rivers
Coal from Semirara
questions.correct: Marble from Romblon

questions.text: A community debates a new open-pit mine. Which consideration is MOST important for their health?
options: Whether acid and metals reach their water
Whether the mine has a nice company logo
Whether workers wear matching uniforms
Whether the mine office is fully air-conditioned
questions.correct: Whether acid and metals reach their water

questions.text: Which agency monitors earthquakes and tsunamis in the Philippines?
options: PHIVOLCS
PAGASA (DOST)
DPWH-Bureau
DENR-EMB
questions.correct: PHIVOLCS

questions.text: What is the epicenter of an earthquake?
options: The surface point above the focus
The deepest point of the fault
The place where the tsunami hits
The machine recording the shaking
questions.correct: The surface point above the focus

questions.text: What causes most volcanic eruptions to be explosive?
options: Gas pressure building in thick magma
Cold rain falling into the crater
Wind blowing over the volcano's top
Sunlight heating the volcano's slopes
questions.correct: Gas pressure building in thick magma

questions.text: What is saltwater intrusion?
options: Seawater moving into fresh groundwater
Salt rain falling over the high mountains
Rivers carrying salt from the land
Fish adding salt to coastal wells
questions.correct: Seawater moving into fresh groundwater

questions.text: PHIVOLCS raises a volcano to Alert Level 3 near your relatives' town. What should they do?
options: Prepare to evacuate; follow LGU advice
Climb the volcano to see the crater glow
Ignore it until Alert Level 5 is raised
Move closer so they can watch the eruption
questions.correct: Prepare to evacuate; follow LGU advice

questions.text: A province had both a strong earthquake and landslides in the same week, though it did not rain. What is the MOST likely link?
options: Shaking loosened slopes and triggered slides
The landslides caused the earthquake later
Earthquakes always bring heavy rain clouds over towns
Landslides only happen when it is very dry
questions.correct: Shaking loosened slopes and triggered slides

questions.text: In which direction do typhoons spin in the Northern Hemisphere?
options: Counterclockwise
Clockwise
Straight line
They do not spin
questions.correct: Counterclockwise

questions.text: Why are storm surges especially dangerous in shallow bays?
options: Water piles up higher as it moves inland
Shallow water absorbs all wave energy
Bays push the whole typhoon back out to sea
Storm surges only happen in deep water
questions.correct: Water piles up higher as it moves inland

questions.text: What triggers most landslides in the Philippines?
options: Heavy or long rain soaking slopes
Strong sunlight drying the soil
Cold winds blowing down from the mountains
Fog forming in the morning
questions.correct: Heavy or long rain soaking slopes

questions.text: Why should you avoid walking through floodwater?
options: It can sweep you away and spread disease
It is always too cold for the skin
It makes the flood rise even faster than before
It turns into salt water when touched
questions.correct: It can sweep you away and spread disease

questions.text: A tropical depression with weak winds is expected to stall over your province for two days. Which hazard should you prepare for MOST?
options: Floods and landslides from heavy rain
Extreme wind damage to tall buildings
A tsunami from the slow-moving storm
Snowfall on the lowland rice fields
questions.correct: Floods and landslides from heavy rain

questions.text: Two typhoons have the same wind speed. Typhoon P moves fast; Typhoon Q moves slowly. Which likely causes MORE flooding, and why?
options: Q — it rains on the same area for longer
P — fast typhoons carry more rainwater
Both equal — speed has no effect at all
P — fast storms always create storm surges
questions.correct: Q — it rains on the same area for longer

questions.text: What is a hazard?
options: An event that could cause harm
A disaster that already happened
A rescue team in a barangay
A shelter for evacuated families
questions.correct: An event that could cause harm

questions.text: Which describes an ipo-ipo?
options: A small, spinning column of air
A slow, rising flood in a river
A crack in the ground after a quake
A long period of very hot days
questions.correct: A small, spinning column of air

questions.text: How have humans modified landforms since the Neolithic?
options: By farming, building, mining and reclaiming land
Only by planting forests on every mountain
Not at all — landforms change only naturally
Only by moving glaciers in the far polar regions
questions.correct: By farming, building, mining and reclaiming land

questions.text: Which activity REDUCES flood and landslide risk?
options: Watershed reforestation
Quarrying hillsides
Filling in coastal wetlands
Cutting mangroves
questions.correct: Watershed reforestation

questions.text: Flooding in a city worsened after many wetlands and creeks were filled for subdivisions. What is the BEST explanation?
options: Less space remained to store and drain water
Subdivisions attract more rainfall to the city
Filled creeks make the rain fall more slowly
Wetlands were the cause of floods all along
questions.correct: Less space remained to store and drain water

questions.text: A barangay can fund only one project. Which BEST reduces long-term typhoon and flood risk?
options: Replanting mangroves and uplands; clear drains
A larger stage for the barangay fiesta
A new paved parking lot right beside the river bank
Painting the barangay hall a new color
questions.correct: Replanting mangroves and uplands; clear drains

questions.text: Which agency developed the iHeatMap?
options: PAGASA
PHIVOLCS
DOH
DENR
questions.correct: PAGASA

questions.text: What category is a heat index of 52 °C or higher?
options: Extreme Danger
Caution
Extreme Caution
Danger
questions.correct: Extreme Danger

questions.text: Why do cities often have higher heat index values than rural areas?
options: Concrete and asphalt store heat
Cities are closer to the Sun
Rural areas have more paved roads
Trees in cities produce heat
questions.correct: Concrete and asphalt store heat

questions.text: Which symptom suggests heat stroke rather than mild fatigue?
options: Confusion and very hot skin
Feeling slightly thirsty
Mild tiredness after a day's work
Wanting to rest in shade
questions.correct: Confusion and very hot skin

questions.text: How does the iHeatMap help an outdoor worker?
options: Shows the hottest hours to avoid
Predicts typhoon landfall points
Measures river levels in his town
Lists earthquake-safe buildings
questions.correct: Shows the hottest hours to avoid

questions.text: The iHeatMap shows Danger-level heat from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. tomorrow. When should a barangay hold its clean-up drive?
options: Early, before 9 a.m.
From 12 noon to 2 p.m.
At 1 p.m. for one hour
During the hottest hour
questions.correct: Early, before 9 a.m.

questions.text: Which law is the Philippine DRRM Act?
options: RA 7942 (mining)

questions.text: What is a Go Bag?
options: A 72-hour emergency supply kit
A school bag for new books
A bag for collecting garbage outside
A gift bag for relief donors
questions.correct: A 72-hour emergency supply kit

questions.text: Which thematic area includes rebuilding homes and restoring livelihoods?
options: Rehabilitation/Recovery
Prevention and Mitigation
Preparedness
Response
questions.correct: Rehabilitation/Recovery

questions.text: Why should a family plan include a meeting point?
options: Members can find each other if separated
It is where the Go Bag is thrown away
It is required for getting a new passport
It is where the typhoon is expected
questions.correct: Members can find each other if separated

questions.text: After a flood, a barangay rebuilds houses in the same flood zone using the same weak materials. What is the problem?
options: Risk stays high; no building back better
Nothing; rebuilding the very same way is ideal
Flood zones become safe after one flood
New houses always attract fewer floods
questions.correct: Risk stays high; no building back better

questions.text: Your class designs a school DRRM plan for earthquakes. Which set of parts is MOST complete?
options: Hazard map, drills, routes, roles, first-aid kits
Class picture, school song, uniform rules, canteen menu
Only a poster saying 'Be careful during earthquakes'
Only a phone number for the principal's office
questions.correct: Hazard map, drills, routes, roles, first-aid kits
